0.long_answer: Systemic primary carnitine deficiency impairs the transport of carnitine into tissues, which in turn prevents the efficient shuttling of long-chain fatty acids into the mitochondria. Normally, carnitine facilitates the transport of these fatty acids across the mitochondrial membranes, ultimately delivering them into the mitochondrial matrix where β-oxidation takes place. Without adequate carnitine, the fatty acids are not properly delivered into the matrix, leading to reduced oxidation and energy production.
